title: Fanout-induced tokens/sec collapse impacting hosted and private customers
creator: Ava Chen
description: Multiple customers reported sudden degradation in tokens/sec and increased TTFT across Hosted and Private deployments starting 2026-03-10 01:12 UTC. Symptoms: first-token delays that grow with model fanout and long-context requests; throughput collapse for multi-tenant fanout > 6; observable spikes in KV cache miss rate and prefetch queue depth after a scheduler batching heuristic change rolled in runtime-2.5.0. Impact affects text-generation and chat endpoints across curated open models and a small set of enterprise quantized variants. This ticket tracks triage, immediate mitigations, and follow-up work to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady fanout of 8 parallel prompts against hosted runtime using model X-2.1 with sequence length ~2048 and priming tokens. 2) Observe initial token emission then long pause (5-12s) before burst; tokens/sec drops by 70% compared to baseline. 3) Reproduce on private VPC cluster with same model and tenant weights pinned; reproduce only when mixture of long-context and short-context requests co-exist and kernel selector chooses large microbatch path. 4) Capture debug traces from scheduler, prefetch, and KV cache windows to confirm prefetch backlog and eviction thrash.
mitigation_actions:
- 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC: Emergency rollback of batching-heuristic change in region us-west-2 (hosted) via runtime-2.5.0 -> runtime-2.4.9 rollback.
- 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: Deployed temporary circuit-breaker limiting per-tenant fanout to 6 for Dedicated and Private clusters (gradual rollout).
- 2026-03-11 09:10 UTC: Disabled background KV prefetch for mixed-length workloads in runtime-2.5.1 candidate while we investigate memory-pressure interplay.
- 2026-03-12 17:45 UTC: Enabled kernel-fallback path that prefers smaller microbatches for long-context requests (PR linked).
Outcome: immediate tokens/sec recovered to within 5-10% of baseline for affected customers; incident mitigation remains active while permanent fix is developed.

comments: 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC - Diego Morales: Pager alerted on TTFT SLOs in us-west-2. Initial triage points to new batching heuristic merged in runtime-2.5.0 (PR #4632). Oncall and SRE paged in.
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - Priya Patel (SRE): Reproduced locally with fanout=8 and long-context mix. KV prefetch queue depth grew unbounded and eviction churn observed. Hit rates dropped from 92% to 47%.
2026-03-10 03:25 UTC - Diego Morales: Rolled back batching heuristic in hosted region; latency partially recovered. Opening ticket to coordinate dedicated/private mitigations.

2026-03-10 05:10 UTC - Maya Gupta (Account Exec): Notified three impacted customers (ACME, NovaHealth, FinLedger). ACME reported degraded UX during peak hours; assigned CSMs to notify when mitigations are live.

2026-03-11 10:30 UTC - Ava Chen: Deployed KV prefetch disable flag to candidate runtime-2.5.1 and saw tokens/sec improvement in canary tenants. Need kernel fallback for full recovery under mixed workloads.

2026-03-12 18:00 UTC - Diego Morales: Kernel-fallback rollout started; monitoring shows stable TTFT and tokens/sec back to baseline for 90% of affected tenants. Continuing verification on private clusters.
2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - SRE Team: Added temporary alert thresholds for KV prefetch backlog and per-tenant fanout ratio to catch regressions earlier.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tokens/sec and first-token latency for affected models return to within 10% of pre-incident baselines across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments.
2) Regression test added to perf harness to simulate mixed-length fanout workloads and assert no tokens/sec collapse.
3) Permanent scheduler heuristic or prefetch strategy implemented with benchmarked improvements and reviewed by runtime and SRE.
4) Customer communications completed and CSMs confirm restored SLA expectations.
resolution_summary: Partial mitigation completed: rollback of the heuristic and temporary disabling of background KV prefetch restored throughput for most customers; kernel-fallback further stabilized emission rates. Root cause traced to an interaction between the new batching heuristic (favoring larger microbatches) and KV prefetch memory/eviction behavior under mixed-context workloads, which caused prefetch backlog and eviction thrashing leading to token emission stalls. Permanent fix will involve a scheduler-weighted fanout cap, smarter prefetch pacing, and targeted unit/regression tests.
tests_and_validation:
- Add workloadized perf test simulating mixed short+long requests with fanout up to 12 to CI perf harness.
- Run end-to-end canary against hosted us-west-2 and a private lab cluster before cutting release.
- Validate KV hit/miss and prefetch queue metrics under synthetic load for at least 6 hours.
notes: This regression surfaced only under mixed workloads (long primed contexts plus short interactive queries). Prioritizing a repair that preserves throughput improvements seen with the original batching heuristic while avoiding prefetch/eviction pathology. Coordinate with Solutions Eng to identify any customers on pinned quantized variants that need out-of-band remediation.
